title: Common-stage descent of localization data and cross-stage orthogonality
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $T=X,U,Z$ use the raw rational categories $D^b_c(T,E)$ for finite coefficient extensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ contained in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and their common-stage category $D^b_c(T,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, with objects $(E,K)$ and morphisms represented over a common finite extension [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Write $T^T_{L/E}$ for scalar extension and $q_{E,T}$ for the finite-stage inclusion.

The canonical scalar comparisons for $i^*,j^*,i_*,j_!$ and their adjunctions descend to exact functors and adjunctions $j_!\dashv j^*$, $i^*\dashv i_*$ on these common-stage categories, with operations as specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], [def-weil-derived-direct-image], [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Their units and counits are represented by the finite-stage units and counits. They obey the unit, associator and shift comparisons of scalar extension; in particular these constructions are independent of further enlargement of the representing field.

If a finite-stage distinguished triangle completes the open counit and closed unit for $K\in D^b_c(X,E)$, its image under $q_{E,X}$ is distinguished and completes the prescribed maps for $(E,K)$. Every object of the common-stage category is of this form, after enlarging $E$ when necessary. For objects represented at possibly different stages, $N=(E,N_E)$ on $U$, $M=(F,M_F)$ on $Z$, and every $m\in\mathbf Z$, the comparison of Hom groups is
$$\operatorname{Hom}(j_!N[m],i_*M)\cong\varinjlim_{L\supset E,F}\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(X,L)}\bigl(j_!T^U_{L/E}N_E[m],i_*T^Z_{L/F}M_F\bigr)=0.$$
Here the transition maps are scalar extension with the canonical functor comparisons; every group in the displayed colimit is zero. These assertions apply to all common-stage morphisms, including those not represented at either original field. No Karoubi completion or claim of a single integral lattice for arbitrary common-stage data is included.

proof.text: At every common field rational orthogonality makes the operation-shifted Hom group a subsingleton. The canonical source and target isomorphisms induce Iso.homCongr, so every raw representative group is a subsingleton. Every raw direct-limit element is represented and therefore zero; the existing Hom coordinate equivalence makes all raw arrows agree. The shifted-pair isomorphism gives the desired shifted Hom vanishing. Every element of the displayed operation direct limit is likewise zero. The unique additive equivalence of the zero groups satisfies the representative formula, and the directed-system equations hold in the subsingleton targets.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q56-fb5ecc807 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all eight steps in full, along with every cited node statement and the main-20261015 'Algebraically closed stage' paragraph of prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages.proof.md. The delivery adds no new nodes. The only statement change replaces 'finite fields E ⊂ Q̄_ℓ' with 'finite coefficient extensions E/Q_ℓ ⊂ Q̄_ℓ'. That is correct: a field of finite cardinality has characteristic ℓ and cannot sit inside Q̄_ℓ, and the new wording matches def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients. Nothing is weakened. Not citing prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors, prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension and thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms is justified. Those nodes are stated for P_T over def-weil-pbc-rational-category, the PBC integral category, while the item works with raw rationalizations of def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed. lem-fd-common-stage-comparison-descent shows that comparing the two needs explicit equivalences, so a direct citation would be a C4 error. The abstract lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent is a correct black-box tool for the same descent. I accept the declared tool_uses: lem-fix-operation-reduction, scalar-extension exactness and the pair-descent lemma. Step by step: (1) the rational sibling's hypotheses match exactly (X separated finite type over F̄_q, ℓ≠p, raw rationalization) and it gives Hom(j_!N[m],i_*M)=0 for arbitrary rational objects. (2) lem-fix-operation-reduction covers rationalization and the common-stage transitions of the cited definition, with identity and tower equations and preservation of units and counits; (j,id_X) gives j_! by the compact-support definition; the degreewise shift argument is concrete. (3) The descent formula b⁻¹Φ(u)b matches the item, and the T_{E/E} unitor normalization is an elementary re-presentation. (4) q_L(A_LΔ_L)=A(q_LΔ_L) on the nose, so exactness follows from the definition of distinguished triangles. (5) The compatible-transformation clause is satisfied, so the triangle identities descend. (6) The finite-stage triangle image is conditional, and its existence is supplied by the parent. (7) a_L/b_L conjugation is compatible with transitions by the tower equations. (8) Every colimit element has a representative at some stage, where the group is zero. Edge cases checked: E=F=L, N or M zero, U or Z empty, negative m, the EF upper bound, and morphisms first represented at a larger field. No duplicates: prop-sf-localization-all-stages, lem-fd-common-stage-comparison-descent, def-weil-operation-exchange-coefficient-descent and the sbc coherence nodes all state different things. Advisories: the associator pentagon is proved only in the proof of lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition, but the cited definition presupposes it; the report mentions a citations.json that is not on the branch.

theorem sfQbarLocalizationCommonStage
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    {Z U : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (hij : Set.range i.base = (Set.range j.base)ᶜ) :
    letI : Z.Over (Spec (.of D.k)) := ⟨i ≫ X ↘ Spec (.of D.k)⟩
    letI : U.Over (Spec (.of D.k)) := ⟨j ≫ X ↘ Spec (.of D.k)⟩
    letI : i.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k)) := ⟨rfl⟩
    letI : j.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k)) := ⟨rfl⟩
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian
      (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))
    letI : CompactSpace X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace
      (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))
    letI : IsNoetherian X := {}
    letI : TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace U := j.isOpenEmbedding.isInducing.noetherianSpace
    letI : TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace Z := i.isEmbedding.isInducing.noetherianSpace
    letI : QuasiCompact j := inferInstance
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Z ↘ Spec (.of D.k)) := inferInstanceAs
      (LocallyOfFiniteType (i ≫ X ↘ Spec (.of D.k)))
    letI : QuasiCompact (Z ↘ Spec (.of D.k)) := inferInstance
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType (U ↘ Spec (.of D.k)) := inferInstanceAs
      (LocallyOfFiniteType (j ≫ X ↘ Spec (.of D.k)))
    letI : QuasiCompact (U ↘ Spec (.of D.k)) := inferInstance
    letI : ∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x) :=
      sfQbarLocalizationResidueInvertible l D hl X (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))
    letI : ∀ z : Z, Invertible (l : Z.residueField z) :=
      sfQbarLocalizationResidueInvertible l D hl Z (Z ↘ Spec (.of D.k))
    letI : ∀ t : U, Invertible (l : U.residueField t) :=
      sfQbarLocalizationResidueInvertible l D hl U (U ↘ Spec (.of D.k))
    Nonempty (SfQbarLocalizationDescent l Ω D hl i j)
